front_content:
**C**: Absorption of $\text{SO}_3$ into conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ forms oleum, which is diluted to produce Sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$)[span_313](start_span)[span_313](end_span).

---

### Question 30
Which one of the following is an alloy composed of 87% copper, 10% tin, and 3% zinc?[span_314](start_span)[span_314](end_span)
back_definition:
Correct Answer: (A)

Explanation: **[span_320](start_span)[span_320](end_span) * **Gun metal** (red brass) is composed of 87% $\text{Cu}$, 10% $\text{Sn}$, and 3% $\text{Zn}$[span_321](start_span)[span_321](end_span). * Bronze is predominantly $\text{Cu} + \text{Sn}$[span_322](start_span)[span_322](end_span). * Solder is $\text{Pb} + \text{Sn}$[span_323](start_span)[span_323](end_span). --- ### Question 31 What is the pH of a solution when the concentration of hydroxide ion is $1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ M}$?[span_324](start_span)[span_324](end_span) a. 5[span_325](start_span)[span_325](end_span) b. 1.8[span_326](start_span)[span_326](end_span) c. 9[span_327](start_span)[span_327](end_span) d. 7[span_328](start_span)[span_328](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_329](start_span)[span_329](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_330](start_span)[span_330](end_span) $$\text{pOH} = -\log[\text{OH}^-] = -\log (1.0 \times 10^{-9}) = 9$$[span_331](start_span)[span_331](end_span) $$\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = 14 \implies \text{pH} = 14 - 9 = 5$$[span_332](start_span)[span_332](end_span) --- ### Question 32 A chemistry teacher designed an experiment to fill three similar balloons with three different gases to compare their rate of diffusion[span_333](start_span)[span_333](end_span). He/she filled the first balloon with helium gas, the second with hydrogen gas, and the third with oxygen gas[span_334](start_span)[span_334](end_span). Which balloon will fill first?[span_335](start_span)[span_335](end_span) a. Second balloon[span_336](start_span)[span_336](end_span) b. Third balloon[span_337](start_span)[span_337](end_span) c. First balloon[span_338](start_span)[span_338](end_span) d. First and second balloon fill equally[span_339](start_span)[span_339](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_340](start_span)[span_340](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_341](start_span)[span_341](end_span) According to Graham's Law of Effusion/Diffusion: $$\text{Rate} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$$[span_342](start_span)[span_342](end_span) Molar masses: $M(\text{H}_2) = 2\text{ g/mol}$, $M(\text{He}) = 4\text{ g/mol}$, $M(\text{O}_2) = 32\text{ g/mol}$[span_343](start_span)[span_343](end_span). Hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) has the lowest molar mass, thus it diffuses fastest and fills the balloon quickest[span_344](start_span)[span_344](end_span). --- ### Question 33 Oxygen reacts with sulfur to form sulfur dioxide[span_345](start_span)[span_345](end_span). Experimentally, it was found that the total mass of reactants (oxygen and sulfur) is equal to the mass of the product (sulfur dioxide)[span_346](start_span)[span_346](end_span). Which of the following laws illustrates this experiment? The law of:[span_347](start_span)[span_347](end_span) a. constant composition[span_348](start_span)[span_348](end_span) b. conservation of mass[span_349](start_span)[span_349](end_span) c. multiple proportions[span_350](start_span)[span_350](end_span) d. definite proportions[span_351](start_span)[span_351](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_352](start_span)[span_352](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_353](start_span)[span_353](end_span) The **Law of Conservation of Mass** (Lavoisier) states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants[span_354](start_span)[span_354](end_span). --- ### Question 34 Which of the following is formed from the combination of two or more substances with at least two visible phases?[span_355](start_span)[span_355](end_span) a. Heterogeneous mixture[span_356](start_span)[span_356](end_span) b. Compound[span_357](start_span)[span_357](end_span) c. Homogeneous mixture[span_358](start_span)[span_358](end_span) d. Solution[span_359](start_span)[span_359](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_360](start_span)[span_360](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_361](start_span)[span_361](end_span) A **heterogeneous mixture** is non-uniform in composition and consists of physically distinct parts or phases (two or more visible phases)[span_362](start_span)[span_362](end_span). Homogeneous mixtures/solutions have a single uniform phase[span_363](start_span)[span_363](end_span). --- ### Question 35 If a $50\text{ cm}^3$ sample of gas exerts a pressure of $60.0\text{ kPa}$ at $35^\circ\text{C}$, what volume will it occupy at STP ($0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm} = 101.325\text{ kPa}$) in $\text{cm}^3$?[span_364](start_span)[span_364](end_span) a. 226.86[span_365](start_span)[span_365](end_span) b. 234.0[span_366](start_span)[span_366](end_span) c. 26.24[span_367](start_span)[span_367](end_span) d. 265.0[span_368](start_span)[span_368](end_span) **Answer:** C[span_369](start_span)[span_369](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_370](start_span)[span_370](end_span) Using the Combined Gas Law: $$\frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2}$$[span_371](start_span)[span_371](end_span) * $P_1 = 60.0\text{ kPa}$, $V_1 = 50\text{ cm}^3$, $T_1 = 35 + 273.15 = 308.15\text{ K}$[span_372](start_span)[span_372](end_span) * $P_2 = 101.325\text{ kPa}$, $T_2 = 273.15\text{ K}$[span_373](start_span)[span_373](end_span) $$V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1 T_2}{P_2 T_1} = \frac{(60.0) \times (50) \times (273.15)}{(101.325) \times (308.15)} = \frac{819450}{31223.4} \approx 26.24\text{ cm}^3$$[span_374](start_span)[span_374](end_span) --- ### Question 36 The following polymer structure represents Poly (ethylene terephthalate) (PET):[span_375](start_span)[span_375](end_span) $$\left[ -\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{C}(=\text{O})- \right]_n$$[span_376](start_span)[span_376](end_span) What are the monomers for this condensation polymer?[span_377](start_span)[span_377](end_span) a. Adipic acid and hexamethylene diamine[span_378](start_span)[span_378](end_span) b. Ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid[span_379](start_span)[span_379](end_span) c. Ethylene glycol and adipic acid[span_380](start_span)[span_380](end_span) d. Terephthalic acid and hexamethylene diamine[span_381](start_span)[span_381](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_382](start_span)[span_382](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_383](start_span)[span_383](end_span) Poly (ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is synthesized via condensation polymerization between **Ethylene glycol** ($\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$) and **Terephthalic acid** ($\text{HOOC}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COOH}$)[span_384](start_span)[span_384](end_span). --- ### Question 37 Which of the following is the structural/condensed molecular formula of 2-hexanol?[span_385](start_span)[span_385](end_span) a. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$[span_386](start_span)[span_386](end_span) b. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})_2\text{CH}_3$[span_387](start_span)[span_387](end_span) c. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$[span_388](start_span)[span_388](end_span) d. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$[span_389](start_span)[span_389](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_390](start_span)[span_390](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_391](start_span)[span_391](end_span) 2-hexanol is a secondary alcohol containing a 6-carbon chain with the hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) located at carbon-2[span_392](start_span)[span_392](end_span): $$\overset{6}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3-\overset{5}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2-\overset{4}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2-\overset{3}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2-\overset{2}{\text{C}}\text{H}(\text{OH})-\overset{1}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$$[span_393](start_span)[span_393](end_span) --- ### Question 38 Crystal line solids are classified as covalent, ionic, molecular, and metallic crystals[span_394](start_span)[span_394](end_span). Which of the following is an example of a metallic crystal?[span_395](start_span)[span_395](end_span) a. Diamond[span_396](start_span)[span_396](end_span) b. Gold[span_397](start_span)[span_397](end_span) c. $\text{KCl}$[span_398](start_span)[span_398](end_span) d. $\text{CaCO}_3$[span_399](start_span)[span_399](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_400](start_span)[span_400](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_401](start_span)[span_401](end_span) * **Gold ($\text{Au}$)** is a metallic crystal bound by metallic bonding[span_402](start_span)[span_402](end_span). * Diamond is a covalent network crystal[span_403](start_span)[span_403](end_span). * $\text{KCl}$ and $\text{CaCO}_3$ are ionic crystals[span_404](start_span)[span_404](end_span). --- ### Question 39 A Grade-12 student sets up a $\text{Zn-Cu}$ cell containing $1.0\text{ M } \text{ZnSO}_4$ solution and $1.0\text{ M } \text{CuSO}_4$ solution to measure cell potential using a voltmeter[span_405](start_span)[span_405](end_span). What will be the reading of the voltmeter under standard conditions?[span_406](start_span)[span_406](end_span) a. $0.34\text{ V}$[span_407](start_span)[span_407](end_span) b. $0.76\text{ V}$[span_408](start_span)[span_408](end_span) c. $0.42\text{ V}$[span_409](start_span)[span_409](end_span) d. $1.1\text{ V}$[span_410](start_span)[span_410](end_span) **Answer:** D[span_411](start_span)[span_411](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_412](start_span)[span_412](end_span) Standard reduction potentials: * $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}$[span_413](start_span)[span_413](end_span) * $E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}$[span_414](start_span)[span_414](end_span) $$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = (+0.34\text{ V}) - (-0.76\text{ V}) = +1.10\text{ V}$$[span_415](start_span)[span_415](end_span) --- ### Question 40 Which of the following factors does NOT affect preferential discharge during electrolysis?[span_416](start_span)[span_416](end_span) a. Nature of ions[span_417](start_span)[span_417](end_span) b. Nature of electrodes[span_418](start_span)[span_418](end_span) c. Thickness of the electrodes[span_419](start_span)[span_419](end_span) d. Concentration of ions[span_420](start_span)[span_420](end_span) **Answer:** C[span_421](start_span)[span_421](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_422](start_span)[span_422](end_span) Preferential discharge of ions at elect rodes depends on: 1. Position in the electrochemical series (nature of ions)[span_423](start_span)[span_423](end_span). 2. Relative concentration of ions in solution[span_424](start_span)[span_424](end_span). 3. Nature/type of electrode material (inert vs. active)[span_425](start_span)[span_425](end_span). **Thickness** of the elect rodes affects resistance/lifespan but does not alter electrochemical selective discharge energy[span_426](start_span)[span_426](end_span). --- ### Question 41 A given element 'M' has an atomic number of 20[span_427](start_span)[span_427](end_span). What is the common ion form of this element after ionization?[span_428](start_span)[span_428](end_span) a. $\text{M}^+$[span_429](start_span)[span_429](end_span) b. $\text{M}^{2+}$[span_430](start_span)[span_430](end_span) c. $\text{M}^-$[span_431](start_span)[span_431](end_span) d. $\text{M}^{2-}$[span_432](start_span)[span_432](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_433](start_span)[span_433](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_434](start_span)[span_434](end_span) Element $M$ ($Z=20$) is Calcium ($\text{Ca}$), a Group IIA alkaline earth metal[span_435](start_span)[span_435](end_span). It has 2 valence electrons ($4s^2$) which it readily loses to achieve a noble gas configuration ($\text{Ar}$), forming the cat i on **$\text{M}^{2+}$**[span_436](start_span)[span_436](end_span). --- ### Question 42 Which one of the following periods is a short period in the modern periodic table?[span_437](start_span)[span_437](end_span) a. Period 5[span_438](start_span)[span_438](end_span) b. Period 3[span_439](start_span)[span_439](end_span) c. Period 4[span_440](start_span)[span_440](end_span) d. Period 6[span_441](start_span)[span_441](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_442](start_span)[span_442](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_443](start_span)[span_443](end_span) Periods 1, 2, and 3 contain 2, 8, and 8 elements respectively and are classified as **short periods**[span_444](start_span)[span_444](end_span). Periods 4, 5, 6, and 7 contain transition elements and inner-transition elements and are long periods[span_445](start_span)[span_445](end_span). --- ### Question 43 What is the reaction type that involves the breaking down of a single compound into two or more components?[span_446](start_span)[span_446](end_span) a. Decomposition reaction[span_447](start_span)[span_447](end_span) b. Redox reaction[span_448](start_span)[span_448](end_span) c. Displacement reaction[span_449](start_span)[span_449](end_span) d. Combination reaction[span_450](start_span)[span_450](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_451](start_span)[span_451](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_452](start_span)[span_452](end_span) A **decomposition reaction** is defined by the general chemical form: $$\text{AB} \right arrow \text{A} + \text{B}$$ where a single reactant breaks down into simpler products[span_453](start_span)[span_453](end_span). --- ### Question 44 A student carried out an experiment to test the reaction between silver nitrate solution and dilute hydrochloric acid under optimum reaction conditions[span_454](start_span)[span_454](end_span). Which one of the following reactions will be obtained according to the law of conservation of mass?[span_455](start_span)[span_455](end_span) a. $\text{HCl}(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3 (aq) \right arrow \text{AgCl}(s) + \text{HNO}_3 (l)$[span_456](start_span)[span_456](end_span) b. $\text{HCl}(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3 (aq) \right arrow 2\text{AgCl}(s) + \text{HNO}_3 (l)$[span_457](start_span)[span_457](end_span) c. $\text{HCl}(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3 (aq) \right arrow \text{AgCl}(s) + 2\text{HNO}_3 (l)$[span_458](start_span)[span_458](end_span) d. $2\text{HCl}(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3 (aq) \right arrow \text{AgCl}(s) + \text{HNO}_3 (l)$[span_459](start_span)[span_459](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_460](start_span)[span_460](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_461](start_span)[span_461](end_span) The reaction is a double displacement precipitation reaction[span_462](start_span)[span_462](end_span). Balancing atom counts: $$\text{HCl}(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3 (aq) \right arrow \text{AgCl}(s) + \text{HNO}_3 (aq)$$ Option A preserves stoichiometric mass conservation with a $1:1$ molar ratio[span_463](start_span)[span_463](end_span). --- ### Question 45 Which of the following is a non-renewable natural resource?[span_464](start_span)[span_464](end_span) a. Cotton[span_465](start_span)[span_465](end_span) b. Gold[span_466](start_span)[span_466](end_span) c. Silk[span_467](start_span)[span_467](end_span) d. Wood[span_468](start_span)[span_468](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_469](start_span)[span_469](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_470](start_span)[span_470](end_span) * **Gold** is an elemental mineral resource formed geological ages ago; its total Earth quantity is finite, making it non-renewable[span_471](start_span)[span_471](end_span). * Cotton, silk, and wood are renewable biological/agricultural resources[span_472](start_span)[span_472](end_span). --- ### Question 46 Consider the following equilibrium reaction:[span_473](start_span)[span_473](end_span) $$a\text{A} + b\text{B} \rightleftharpoons c\text{C} + d\text{D}$$[span_474](start_span)[span_474](end_span) Which of the following is CORRECT about the given reaction?[span_475](start_span)[span_475](end_span) a. Removing both reactants and products decreases the value of $K_c$.[span_476](start_span)[span_476](end_span) b. Adding products to the system decreases the value of $K_c$.[span_477](start_span)[span_477](end_span) c. Adding reactants to the system increases the value of $K_c$.[span_478](start_span)[span_478](end_span) d. $K_c$ is not affected by removing both reactants and products.[span_479](start_span)[span_479](end_span) **Answer:** D[span_480](start_span)[span_480](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_481](start_span)[span_481](end_span) The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is a thermodynamic constant dependent **solely on temperature**[span_482](start_span)[span_482](end_span). Changing concentration by adding or removing species shifts equilibrium position according to Le Chatelier's Principle but leaves the numeric value of $K_c$ unchanged[span_483](start_span)[span_483](end_span). --- ### Question 47 What is the molecular shape of phosphorus trichloride, $\text{PCl}_3$? (Atomic number $\text{P}=15$, $\text{Cl}=17$)[span_484](start_span)[span_484](end_span) a. Trigonal planar[span_485](start_span)[span_485](end_span) b. Trigonal pyramidal[span_486](start_span)[span_486](end_span) c. Square planar[span_487](start_span)[span_487](end_span) d. It forms 3 single bonds with $\text{Cl}$ atoms and retains 1 lone pair ($\text{AX}_3\text{E}_1$ VSEPR notation)[span_492](start_span)[span_492](end_span). The electron geometry is tetrahedral, giving a **trigonal pyramidal** molecular geometry[span_493](start_span)[span_493](end_span). --- ### Question 48 Consider the reaction curve showing concentration of reactant D over time: ! [Concentration vs Time Graph] (https://i.imgur.com/example_rate_graph.png) *(Graph shows $[\text{D}]$ decreasing non-linearly over time, with Point A earlier on the steep curve and Point B later on the flat tened curve)*[span_494](start_span)[span_494](end_span) Which of the following is CORRECT about the rate of reaction of reactant D?[span_495](start_span)[span_495](end_span) a. As reactant concentration diminishes, collision frequency decreases, causing the rate to slow down[span_503](start_span)[span_503](end_span). The curve is steeper at Point A than at Point B, meaning the instantaneous rate at A is greater[span_504](start_span)[span_504](end_span). --- ### Question 49 Neutron is one of the fundamental sub-atomic particles of an atom[span_505](start_span)[span_505](end_span). What is the relative charge of a neutron in an atom?[span_506](start_span)[span_506](end_span) a. 0[span_507](start_span)[span_507](end_span) b. +1[span_508](start_span)[span_508](end_span) c. -1[span_509](start_span)[span_509](end_span) d. +2[span_510](start_span)[span_510](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_511](start_span)[span_511](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_512](start_span)[span_512](end_span) Neutrons are neutral subatomic particles located in the atomic nucleus with a charge of **0**[span_513](start_span)[span_513](end_span). Protons have +1, electrons -1[span_514](start_span)[span_514](end_span). --- ### Question 50 Consider the following $\text{Zn-Cu}$ voltaic cell diagram: ! The electrode where reduction occurs is the **Cathode** (labeled B)[span_524](start_span)[span_524](end_span). --- ### Question 51 Consider the following structure: $$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$[span_525](start_span)[span_525](end_span) Which one of the following is the IUPAC name for the given organic compound?[span_526](start_span)[span_526](end_span) a. 2-Ethyl-6-heptyne[span_527](start_span)[span_527](end_span) b. 6-Ethyl-3-heptyne[span_528](start_span)[span_528](end_span) c. 3-Methyl-5-octyne[span_529](start_span)[span_529](end_span) d. 6-Methyl-3-octyne[span_530](start_span)[span_530](end_span) **Answer:** D[span_531](start_span)[span_531](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_532](start_span)[span_532](end_span) 1. ### Question 52
! [Iron and Sulfur Reaction] (https://i.imgur.com/example_heating_fe_s.png)
*(Diagram shows a test tube containing iron filings + sulfur being heated over a Bunsen burner flame)*[span_537](start_span)[span_537](end_span) Which of the following reactions takes place in the above experiment?[span_538](start_span)[span_538](end_span)
back_definition:
Correct Answer: (A)

Explanation: **[span_544](start_span)[span_544](end_span) Heating iron filings ($\text{Fe}$) and sulfur powder ($\text{S}$) causes them to combine directly into a single substance, iron (II) sulfide: $$\text{Fe}(s) + \text{S}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{FeS}(s)$$[span_545](start_span)[span_545](end_span) This is a synthesis or **direct combination reaction**[span_546](start_span)[span_546](end_span). --- ### Question 53 An equilibrium mixture contains $0.30\text{ mol }\text{CO}$, $0.10\text{ mol }\text{H}_2$, $0.020\text{ mol }\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and an unknown concentration of $\text{CH}_4$, in a $1.0\text{ L}$ container at $1200\text{ K}$[span_547](start_span)[span_547](end_span). In this mixture, what is the molar concentration of $\text{CH}_4$ at equilibrium?[span_548](start_span)[span_548](end_span) $$\text{CO}(g) + 3\text{H}_2 (g) \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_4 (g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g), \quad K_c = 3.92$$[span_549](start_span)[span_549](end_span) a. $0.059\text{ mol/L}$[span_550](start_span)[span_550](end_span) b. $0.015\text{ mol/L}$[span_551](start_span)[span_551](end_span) c. $0.197\text{ mol/L}$[span_552](start_span)[span_552](end_span) d. $0.001\text{ mol/L}$[span_553](start_span)[span_553](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_554](start_span)[span_554](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_555](start_span)[span_555](end_span) Set up the equilibrium constant expression: $$K_c = \frac{[\text{CH}_4][\text{H}_2\text{O}]}{[\text{CO}][\text{H}_2]^3}$$[span_556](start_span)[span_556](end_span) Substitute given values ($V = 1.0\text{ L}$ means $\text{moles} = \text{molarity}$): $$3.92 = \frac{[\text{CH}_4](0.020)}{(0.30)(0.10)^3} = \frac{0.020 [\text{CH}_4]}{(0.30)(0.001)} = \frac{0.020 [\text{CH}_4]}{0.0003}$$[span_557](start_span)[span_557](end_span) $$0.020 [\text{CH}_4] = 3.92 \times 0.0003 = 0.001176$$[span_558](start_span)[span_558](end_span) $$[\text{CH}_4] = \frac{0.001176}{0.020} = 0.0588\text{ M} \approx 0.059\text{ mol/L}$$[span_559](start_span)[span_559](end_span) --- ### Question 54 Which one of the following is the reason why hydrolysis of sodium carbonate gives a basic solution? This is due to:[span_560](start_span)[span_560](end_span) a. $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ is hydrolyzed[span_561](start_span)[span_561](end_span) b. $\text{H}^+$ is hydrolyzed[span_562](start_span)[span_562](end_span) c. $\text{OH}^-$ is hydrolyzed[span_563](start_span)[span_563](end_span) d. $\text{Na}^+$ is hydrolyzed[span_564](start_span)[span_564](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_565](start_span)[span_565](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_566](start_span)[span_566](end_span) $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ dissolves to release $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$[span_567](start_span)[span_567](end_span). $\text{Na}^+$ is the spectator conjugate of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and does not hydrolyze[span_568](start_span)[span_568](end_span). $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ is the strong conjugate base of a weak acid ($\text{HCO}_3^-$) and undergoes anion hydrolysis[span_569](start_span)[span_569](end_span): $$\text{CO}_3^{2-}(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons \text{HCO}_3^-(aq) + \text{OH}^-(aq)$$ The production of excess $\text{OH}^-$ turns the solution basic[span_570](start_span)[span_570](end_span). --- ### Question 55 The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate during the commercial preparation of lime ($\text{CaO}$) is given below:[span_571](start_span)[span_571](end_span) $$\text{CaCO}_3 (s) \right arrow \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2 (g)$$[span_572](start_span)[span_572](end_span) What is the atom economy for the preparation of lime based on the above reaction? (Atomic masses: $\text{Ca}=40$, $\text{C}=12$, $\text{O}=16\text{ g/mol}$)[span_573](start_span)[span_573](end_span) a. 56%[span_574](start_span)[span_574](end_span) b. 49.1%[span_575](start_span)[span_575](end_span) c. 44%[span_576](start_span)[span_576](end_span) d. 100%[span_577](start_span)[span_577](end_span) **Answer:** A[span_578](start_span)[span_578](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_579](start_span)[span_579](end_span) $$\text{Atom Economy} = \left( \frac{\text{Molar mass of desired product}}{\text{Total molar mass of reactants}} \right) \times 100%$$[span_580](start_span)[span_580](end_span) * Desired product ($\text{CaO}$): $40 + 16 = 56\text{ g/mol}$[span_581](start_span)[span_581](end_span) * Reactant ($\text{CaCO}_3$): $40 + 12 + (3 \times 16) = 100\text{ g/mol}$[span_582](start_span)[span_582](end_span) $$\text{Atom Economy} = \left( \frac{56}{100} \right) \times 100% = 56%$$[span_583](start_span)[span_583](end_span) --- ### Question 56 The rate constant of a reaction increases by a factor of 4 when the temperature is increased from $300\text{ K}$ to $320\text{ K}$[span_584](start_span)[span_584](end_span). What is the approximate activation energy of the reaction? ($R = 8.314\text{ J/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}$, $\ln (4) \approx 1.386$)[span_585](start_span)[span_585](end_span) a. $27.6\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_586](start_span)[span_586](end_span) b. $55.3\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_587](start_span)[span_587](end_span) c. $110.6\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_588](start_span)[span_588](end_span) d. $8.31\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_589](start_span)[span_589](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_590](start_span)[span_590](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_591](start_span)[span_591](end_span) Using the two-temperature Arrhenius equation: $$\ln\left( \frac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \frac{E_a}{R} \left( \frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2} \right)$$[span_592](start_span)[span_592](end_span) $$1.386 = \frac{E_a}{8.314} \left( \frac{1}{300} - \frac{1}{320} \right) = \frac{E_a}{8.314} \left( \frac{20}{96000} \right) = \frac{E_a}{8.314} \left( \frac{1}{4800} \right)$$[span_593](start_span)[span_593](end_span) $$E_a = 1.386 \times 8.314 \times 4800 = 55311.6\text{ J/mol} \approx 55.3\text{ kJ/mol}$$[span_594](start_span)[span_594](end_span) --- ### Question 57 Calculate the electromotive force (EMF) of the cell $\text{Zn}|\text{Zn}^{2+}(0.01\text{M})||\text{Cu}^{2+}(1.0\text{M})|\text{Cu}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V}$)[span_595](start_span)[span_595](end_span). a. $1.10\text{ V}$[span_596](start_span)[span_596](end_span) b. $1.04\text{ V}$[span_597](start_span)[span_597](end_span) c. $1.16\text{ V}$[span_598](start_span)[span_598](end_span) d. $1.22\text{ V}$[span_599](start_span)[span_599](end_span) **Answer:** C[span_600](start_span)[span_600](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_601](start_span)[span_601](end_span) By the Nernst equation ($n=2$): $$E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{n} \log Q = 1.10 - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log \left( \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} \right)$$[span_602](start_span)[span_602](end_span) $$E = 1.10 - 0.0296 \log\left(\frac{0.01}{1.0}\right) = 1.10 - 0.0296 (-2) = 1.10 + 0.0592 = 1.1592\text{ V} \approx 1.16\text{ V}$$[span_603](start_span)[span_603](end_span) --- ### Question 58 What is the pH of a buffer solution prepared by mixing $50.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.20\text{ M } \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and $50.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.10\text{ M } \text{NaOH}$? ($K_a \text{ for } \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$)[span_604](start_span)[span_604](end_span) a. 2.87[span_605](start_span)[span_605](end_span) b. 4.74[span_606](start_span)[span_606](end_span) c. 5.04[span_607](start_span)[span_607](end_span) d. 9.26[span_608](start_span)[span_608](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_609](start_span)[span_609](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_610](start_span)[span_610](end_span) Moles initial: * $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 0.050\text{ L} \times 0.20\text{ M} = 0.010\text{ mol}$[span_611](start_span)[span_611](end_span) * $\text{NaOH} = 0.050\text{ L} \times 0.10\text{ M} = 0.005\text{ mol}$[span_612](start_span)[span_612](end_span) Neutralization reaction: $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{OH}^- \right arrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$ * Remaining $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 0.010 - 0.005 = 0.005\text{ mol}$[span_613](start_span)[span_613](end_span) * Formed $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- = 0.005\text{ mol}$[span_614](start_span)[span_614](end_span) Since $[\text{Acid}] = [\text{Conjugate Base}]$, using Henderson-Hasselbalch: $$\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log\left(\frac{[\text{Base}]}{[\text{Acid}]}\right) = \text{p}K_a + \log (1) = \text{p}K_a$$[span_615](start_span)[span_615](end_span) $$\text{pH} = -\log (1.8 \times 10^{-5}) \approx 4.74$$[span_616](start_span)[span_616](end_span) --- ### Question 59 Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of liquid benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 (l)$) given the standard enthalpies of combustion: $\Delta H_c^\circ(\text{C}(s)) = -394\text{ kJ/mol}$, $\Delta H_c^\circ(\text{H}_2 (g)) = -286\text{ kJ/mol}$, $\Delta H_c^\circ(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 (l)) = -3268\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_617](start_span)[span_617](end_span). a. $-46\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_618](start_span)[span_618](end_span) b. $+46\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_619](start_span)[span_619](end_span) c. $+3222\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_620](start_span)[span_620](end_span) d. $-3268\text{ kJ/mol}$[span_621](start_span)[span_621](end_span) **Answer:** B[span_622](start_span)[span_622](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_623](start_span)[span_623](end_span) Target formation reaction: $6\text{C}(s) + 3\text{H}_2 (g) \right arrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 (l)$[span_624](start_span)[span_624](end_span). Using standard enthalpies of combustion: $$\Delta H_f^\circ = \sum \Delta H_c^\circ(\text{reactants}) - \sum \Delta H_c^\circ(\text{products})$$[span_625](start_span)[span_625](end_span) $$\Delta H_f^\circ = [6(-394) + 3(-286)] - [-3268]$$[span_626](start_span)[span_626](end_span) $$\Delta H_f^\circ = [-2364 - 858] + 3268 = -3222 + 3268 = +46\text{ kJ/mol}$$[span_627](start_span)[span_627](end_span) --- ### Question 60 Which of the following alkyl halides is most reactive towards an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ substitution reaction mechanism?[span_628](start_span)[span_628](end_span) a. 1-Chlorobutane[span_629](start_span)[span_629](end_span) b. 2-Chlorobutane[span_630](start_span)[span_630](end_span) c. 2-Chloro-2-methylpropane[span_631](start_span)[span_631](end_span) d. Chloromethane[span_632](start_span)[span_632](end_span) **Answer:** C[span_633](start_span)[span_633](end_span) **Explanation:**[span_634](start_span)[span_634](end_span) The rate-determining step in an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism is carbocation formation[span_635](start_span)[span_635](end_span). Carbocation stability increases in the order: methyl < $1^\circ < 2^\circ < 3^\circ$ due to alkyl hyperconjugation and inductive stabilization[span_636](start_span)[span_636](end_span). 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is a **tertiary ($3^\circ$) alkyl halide**, making it the most reactive via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$[span_637](start_span)[span_637](end_span). --- ### Question 61 *(Curriculum Addition to complete 80 questions)* Which quantum number determines the spatial orientation of an orbital in a magnetic field? a. Principal quantum number ($n$) b. Azimuthal quantum number ($l$) c. Magnetic quantum number ($m_l$) d. Spin quantum number ($m_s$) **Answer:** C **Explanation:** * **$n$** defines energy level and shell size. * **$l$** defines orbital shape (subshell). * **$m_l$** specifies spatial orientation of the orbital in space relative to an external magnetic field. * **$m_s$** specifies intrinsic electron spin. --- ### Question 62 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the hybridization of the central sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride, $\text{SF}_6$? a. $sp^3$ b. $sp^3d$ c. $sp^3d^2$ d. $sp^2$ **Answer:** C **Explanation:** $\text{SF}_6$ has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around Sulfur (Steric Number = 6). A steric number of 6 corresponds to an octahedral geometry and **$sp^3d^2$** hybridization. --- ### Question 63 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest boiling point elevation? a. $0.10\text{ M } \text{NaCl}$ b. $0.10\text{ M } \text{CaCl}_2$ c. $0.10\text{ M } \text{AlCl}_3$ d. $0.10\text{ M } \text{Glucose}$ **Answer:** C **Explanation:** Boiling point elevation is a colligative property ($\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m$). Higher van 't Hoff factor ($i$) yields higher boiling point: * Glucose: $i = 1$ * $\text{NaCl}$: $i = 2$ ($\text{Na}^+, \text{Cl}^-$) * $\text{CaCl}_2$: $i = 3$ ($\text{Ca}^{2+}, 2\text{Cl}^-$) * **$\text{AlCl}_3$**: $i = 4$ ($\text{Al}^{3+}, 3\text{Cl}^-$) — highest ion concentration. --- ### Question 64 *(Curriculum Addition)* The conjugate base of hydrogen phosphate ion, $\text{HPO}_4^{2-}$, is: a. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ b. $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ c. $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ d. $\text{P}_2\text{O}_7^{4-}$ **Answer:** C **Explanation:** A conjugate base is formed when a Bronsted-Lowry acid removes one proton ($\text{H}^+$). $$\text{HPO}_4^{2-} \right arrow \text{H}^+ + \text{PO}_4^{3-}$$ Thus, the conjugate base is **$\text{PO}_4^{3-}$**. --- ### Question 65 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the oxidation number of chromium in potassium dichromate, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$? a. +3 b. +6 c. +7 d. +4 **Answer:** B **Explanation:** $$2(+1) + 2 (x) + 7(-2) = 0$$ $$2 + 2x - 14 = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6$$ --- ### Question 66 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which of the following primary functional groups characterizes an aldehyde? a. $-\text{COOH}$ b. $-\text{CHO}$ c. $-\text{CO}-$ d. $-\text{OH}$ **Answer:** B **Explanation:** * $-\text{CHO}$ is aldehyde (carbonyl bonded to at least one hydrogen). * $-\text{COOH}$ is carboxylic acid. * $-\text{CO}-$ is ketone. * $-\text{OH}$ is alcohol. --- ### Question 67 *(Curriculum Addition)* In a zero-order reaction, the unit of the rate constant $k$ is: a. $\text{s}^{-1}$ b. $\text{L}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ c. $\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ d. $\text{L}^2\cdot\text{mol}^{-2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ **Answer:** C **Explanation:** $\text{Rate} = k[\text{A}]^0 = k$. Since $\text{Rate}$ is in concentration/time ($\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ or $\text{M/s}$), the unit for $k$ in a zero-order reaction is **$\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$**. --- ### Question 68 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which gas is produced at the anode during the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$) solution using inert elect rodes? a. Oxygen gas ($\text{O}_2$) b. Hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) c. Chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) d. Sodium vapor ($\text{Na}$) **Answer:** C **Explanation:** In concentrated brine, due to overvoltage and concentration effects, chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) are preferentially oxidized over water at the anode, yielding **Chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$)**. Water is reduced at cathode to produce $\text{H}_2$. --- ### Question 69 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the general formula for non-cyclic alkanes? a. $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ b. $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$ c. $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n-2}$ d. $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n-6}$ **Answer:** B **Explanation:** Saturated open-chain hydrocarbons (alkanes) conform to the general molecular formula **$\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$**. --- ### Question 70 *(Curriculum Addition)* According to Le Chatelier's principle, what happens to the exothermic reaction $2\text{SO}_2 (g) + \text{O}_2 (g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3 (g) + \text{heat}$ when temperature is increased? a. Equilibrium shifts to the right; $K_c$ increases. b. Equilibrium shifts to the left; $K_c$ decreases. c. Equilibrium shifts to the right; $K_c$ stays constant. d. No shift occurs. **Answer:** B **Explanation:** Increasing temperature adds heat to an exothermic system. To counter act this, the equilibrium shifts in othermic reverse direction (to the left), forming more reactants and causing **$K_c$ to decrease**. --- ### Question 71 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which oxide listed below is amphoteric? a. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ b. $\text{SO}_3$ c. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ d. $\text{CO}_2$ **Answer:** C **Explanation:** Aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) reacts with both acids and strong bases to yield salt and water, making it **amphoteric**. ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is basic; $\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$ are acidic). --- ### Question 72 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the percentage composition by mass of carbon in ethanol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$? ($\text{C}=12, \text{H}=1, \text{O}=16$) a. 52.2% b. 13.0% c. 34.8% d. 26.1% **Answer:** A **Explanation:** * Molar mass of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O} = (2 \times 12) + (6 \times 1) + 16 = 24 + 6 + 16 = 46\text{ g/mol}$. * Mass of Carbon $= 24\text{ g/mol}$. $$%\text{ C} = \left(\frac{24}{46}\right) \times 100% \approx 52.17% \approx 52.2%$$ --- ### Question 73 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the IUPAC name of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$? a. Propanone b. Butanal c. Butan-2-one d. Butan-1-ol **Answer:** C **Explanation:** It is a 4-carbon chain ketone with the carbonyl oxygen located at position 2: **Butan-2-one** (or 2-butanone). --- ### Question 74 *(Curriculum Addition)* The expression for the solubility product constant ($K_{sp}$) of calcium phosphate, $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$, is: a. $[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{PO}_4^{3-}]$ b. $[\text{Ca}^{2+}]^3 [\text{PO}_4^{3-}]^2$ c. $[\text{Ca}^{2+}]^2 [\text{PO}_4^{3-}]^3$ d. $3[\text{Ca}^{2+}] \cdot 2[\text{PO}_4^{3-}]$ **Answer:** B **Explanation:** Dissolution equation: $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Ca}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{PO}_4^{3-}(aq)$. $$K_{sp} = [\text{Ca}^{2+}]^3 [\text{PO}_4^{3-}]^2$$ --- ### Question 75 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure? a. Charles's Law b. Boyle's Law c. Gay-Lussac's Law d. Avogadro's Law **Answer:** B **Explanation:** **Boyle's Law** states $V \propto \frac{1}{P}$ at constant temperature and amount of gas. --- ### Question 76 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which standard subatomic particle was discovered by J. J. Thomson using the cathode ray tube experiment? a. Proton b. Neutron c. Electron d. Alpha particle **Answer:** C **Explanation:** J. J. Thomson discovered the **electron** in 1897 through his experiments with cathode ray tubes. --- ### Question 77 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the bond angle in a molecule with perfect tetrahedral geometry (such as $\text{CH}_4$)? a. 90° b. 120° c. 109.5° d. 180° **Answer:** C **Explanation:** A regular $sp^3$ hybridized tetrahedral geometry with 0 lone pairs ($\text{AX}_4$) exhibits bond angles of **109.5°**. --- ### Question 78 *(Curriculum Addition)* In industrial extraction of iron in a blast furnace, which species acts as the main reducing agent for iron ores? a. Carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) b. Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) c. Limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$) d. Slag ($\text{CaSiO}_3$) **Answer:** B **Explanation:** Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) gas generated by high-temperature coke reaction reduces hematite ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$): $$\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 3\text{CO} \right arrow 2\text{Fe} + 3\text{CO}_2$$ --- ### Question 79 *(Curriculum Addition)* Which type of radiation possesses the highest penetrating power? a. Alpha ($\alpha$) particles b. Beta ($\beta$) particles c. Gamma ($\gamma$) rays d. Positron emission **Answer:** C **Explanation:** **Gamma ($\gamma$) rays** are high-energy electromagnetic photons with zero charge and mass, giving them the highest penetrating power among nuclear emissions. --- ### Question 80 *(Curriculum Addition)* What is the oxidation product of a secondary alcohol when reacted with potassium dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7/\text{H}^+$)? a. Carboxylic acid b. Aldehyde c. Ketone d. Alkene **Answer:** C **Explanation:** Control led oxidation of a secondary alcohol ($\text{R}_2\text{CHOH}$) removes two hydrogen atoms to yield a **ketone** ($\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O}$). Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes/carboxylic acids.
